title: Step by Step Guide to Reviewing a Manuscript | Wiley

extracted.subtask_description: A granular walkthrough of how a reviewer should check whether conclusions match evidence and whether citations actually support the statements attached to them, section by section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusions well-supported by the evidence presented
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Evaluate whether the authors' conclusions are well-supported by the evidence presented. If the author disagrees significantly with the current academic consensus, do they have a substantial case? If not, what would be required to make their case credible?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames disagreement-with-consensus claims as needing a higher evidentiary bar, and asks the reviewer to specify the missing evidence rather than just reject the claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusions contradicting the evidence (major flaw category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly listed flaw category: 'Conclusions contradicting the evidence' - 'Are the conclusions supported by the data, or do they contradict the author's own statistical or qualitative data?' Major flaws in the data itself: 'Insufficient data,' 'Unclear data tables,' 'Contradictory data that either are not self-consistent or disagree with the conclusions,' and 'Confirmatory data that adds little, if anything, to current understanding - unless strong arguments for such repetition are made.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty/gap claims require recent authoritative citations
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Originality and topicality can only be established in the light of recent authoritative research. For example, it's impossible to argue that there is a conflict in current understanding by referencing articles that are 10 years old.' A claim that 'this gap hasn't been addressed' is only credible if backed by recent citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citing older seminal papers for genuinely foundational methodology is fine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance claims require explicit tie to published literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should 'evaluate the trends observed and explain the significance of the results to wider understanding. This can only be done by referencing published research.' A significance claim requires an explicit tie to the literature, not just internal statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-free conclusions should be sent back for revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusions 'should reflect upon the aims - whether they were achieved or not - and, just like the aims, should not be surprising. If the conclusions are not evidence-based, it's appropriate to ask for them to be re-written.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Data trends must visibly support the discussion and conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should check that 'the trends you can see support the paper's discussion and conclusions' and that 'there is sufficient data' (e.g., enough data points across a time series to support the described trend).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference adequacy: cited sources actually support the manuscript's claims
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Assess the adequacy of the references by determining if they adequately support the manuscript's claims and if there are any significant studies, both similar and opposing, that should be cited but are missing. A reference list that is too sparse or relies heavily on a limited number of sources may indicate that additional references are needed, though avoid judging solely by quantity.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference balance: recognize competing and prior work fairly
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Check for a well-balanced list of references that is helpful to the reader, fair to competing authors, and not over-reliant on self-citation. The references should recognize the initial discoveries and related work that led to the work under assessment.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should be able to evaluate the balance of the references without looking up every single citation but should raise any concerns if certain perspectives seem underrepresented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrary evidence must be cited and addressed, not omitted
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Are the authors presenting findings that challenge current thinking? Is the evidence they present strong enough to prove their case? Have they cited all the relevant work that would contradict their thinking and addressed it appropriately?' An explicit instruction to check that contrary evidence is engaged with, not omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central citations checked for accuracy and format
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Where a cited article is central to the author's argument, you should check the accuracy and format of the reference.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full exhaustive reference-list checking is the editor's job, not the reviewer's.
